survey: Image 5 shows a small two-wheeled covered cart on a dirt road. Main parts: (1) A wooden box bed with a red top rim. The camera is front-left, so the cart is seen in three-quarter view, with the left side and front panel visible. (2) A canvas cover with stitched seams. It arches over the rear and middle of the bed, sits on the red rim, and has an open arched front facing the driver's seat. (3) A plank driver's seat on two short posts at the front of the bed, just ahead of the canvas opening. (4) Two large spoked wheels on one axle, with the hub below the bed floor. The near wheel has a red hub and a black cap. The far wheel is partly hidden and sits behind and to the right of the near wheel, where the axle's angle in this view puts it. Both wheels touch the ground and cast matching shadows. (5) A single wooden tongue that leaves the underside of the bed's front, angles down and forward, and rests on the ground on a short crossbar. That makes the cart a stable three-point stand when unhitched. Every part attaches where it should, the cart's weight is properly supported, and the two wheels match in size and spoke style. The missing visible axle and harness hitch are acceptable simplifications.
